title: A 1,000-Year Wooden Tower With Zero Nails | China Travel Expert
description:
How does a wooden tower survive nearly 1,000 years and dozens of earthquakes — without a single nail?

The Sakyamuni Pagoda at Fogong Temple in Yingxian, Shanxi, was built in 1056 during the Liao dynasty. At 67.31 meters it is the oldest and tallest surviving all-wood pagoda on Earth (Guinness World Records, 2016). It is held together entirely by mortise-and-tenon joinery and tens of thousands of interlocking bracket sets — no nails, no glue, no metal. That flexible wooden frame lets the tower sway slightly and absorb seismic shocks, which is why it has outlasted centuries of quakes. From outside it reads as five storeys; hidden mezzanines make nine internal levels.

🧭 Expert Tip: Arrive right at sunrise — low golden light rakes across the old larch timber and the courtyard is still empty.

一座木塔，近千年，没用一颗钉子。
